answer: Agents resist Sybil by requiring each identity to periodically post a beacon that embeds a fresh sequential memory-hard proof bound to its unique mesa of prior state hashes. An attacker creating N clones must recompute the full working set for every identity independently at the wharf of each epoch close; the sequential nature and non-shareable cache force linear compute cost in N rather than constant wall-clock time, making large farms economically prohibitive.
